title: Control-to-Evidence Mapping: Retention Controls + Audit Logging (SOC 2 / ISO-aligned)
author: Olga Petrov
body:
## Purpose
This page maps **Retention Controls** and **Audit Logging** capabilities to common audit criteria (SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria and ISO 27001-style requirements) and specifies:
- What evidence exists (artifacts, screenshots, exports, logs, configs)
- Where it lives (Confluence, systems of record, dashboards)
- Who owns it (RACI-style owner + backup)
- How to verify it (repeatable verification steps)

This mapping is used for:
- Enterprise security reviews (customer evidence requests)
- Internal SOC 2 / ISO-aligned evidence collection
- Ongoing control operation verification (quarterly/annual checks)

---

## Scope
### In scope (v1)
- Tenant-configurable **retention policies** for eligible datasets (audit logs, admin activity, selected telemetry/analytics, selected operational logs where applicable)
- **Retention enforcement** (scheduled deletion jobs and/or datastore TTLs) with monitoring and auditability
- **Audit logging coverage** for administrative and security-relevant actions (including changes to retention policies, legal holds, and export configuration)
- **Legal hold and exceptions workflow** (approval, documentation, periodic review)
- **Audit log exports** and statement of retention boundaries for exports

### Out of scope / constraints (documented)
- Full customer-configurable retention across every internal infrastructure log stream (governed by SRE standards/vendor constraints)
- Customer-configurable retention for all raw inference payload content (depends on broader data handling choices)

---

## Definitions
- **Retention policy**: Tenant-scoped configuration specifying how long eligible data types are retained, with guardrails (min/max), environment/region applicability, and overrides.
- **Enforcement**: Mechanism that deletes/compacts data once it exceeds retention (e.g., partition TTL, scheduled deletes, compaction jobs).
- **Legal hold**: A flag preventing deletion for certain tenants/datasets regardless of retention policy, until hold is removed through approved workflow.
- **Audit log**: Immutable, append-only record of security/admin events (who did what, when, where, and outcome) used for investigations and compliance.

---

## Systems of record (where evidence typically lives)
- **Confluence (Security & Compliance)**: policy docs, ADRs, runbooks, evidence procedures, compliance reporting pack
- **Redwood Console**: effective retention policy view, last enforcement run status, legal hold banners, audit log viewer/export UX
- **Control plane service** (internal): retention policy config store + evaluation engine (tenant/org/env/region precedence)
- **Audit log service**: append-only audit log store + export service
- **Telemetry/analytics pipeline**: eligible analytic tables with TTL/partition expiry
- **Observability stack**: dashboards/alerts for enforcement jobs and deletion lag
- **Ticketing systems**: exception/hold approvals and periodic review records

Note: Exact storage backends vary by deployment mode (Hosted/Dedicated/Private). Verification should follow the deployment-specific instructions in the runbook.

---

## Control mapping table
The table below is intentionally **SOC 2 / ISO-aligned** (not a literal SOC 2 report). Auditors/customers may map these to their preferred frameworks.

Legend:
- **Frequency**: recommended evidence collection cadence
- **Owner**: functional owner of the control operation + evidence availability

| Control area | SOC 2 / ISO reference (examples) | Control intent | Evidence artifacts (what) | Evidence location (where) | Owner | Frequency | Verification steps (how) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Retention policy definition + guardrails | SOC2 CC2.1, CC5.2; ISO 27001 A.5.1, A.8.2 | Retention is defined, approved, and constrained by guardrails (min/max; disallow unsafe “never delete” unless explicitly permitted) | (1) Retention Controls Overview page; (2) policy schema spec w/ examples; (3) ADR: enforcement strategy; (4) screenshot/export of guardrail configuration | Confluence: retention overview + schema spec + ADR | Naomi Feldman (Product, Security & Compliance) / Marcus Lin (Security Eng) | Annual + on major change | Confirm documentation includes: eligible datasets list, default retention, min/max constraints, legal hold semantics, and deployment differences. Validate schema includes guardrail validation behavior and disallowed values. |
| Tenant-configurable retention settings | SOC2 CC6.6, CC7.2; ISO 27001 A.9, A.12.1 | Authorized tenant admins can view and change retention within allowed bounds, with transparency of effective policy | (1) Console screenshots of retention settings page + effective policy view; (2) API docs/endpoint contract; (3) audit events for changes | Redwood Console (admin UI); Confluence/API docs; audit log viewer | Chloe Martin (Console) / Jada Williams (Console backend) | Quarterly sample | Using a test tenant: (a) view current effective policy; (b) attempt update within bounds (succeeds); (c) attempt update outside bounds (fails with clear error); (d) confirm change appears in admin audit trail. |
| Policy precedence & determinism | SOC2 CC7.2; ISO 27001 A.12.1.2 | Effective retention is computed consistently with documented precedence (org/tenant/env/region) and is deterministic | (1) Policy evaluation spec; (2) golden tests evidence (test output excerpt); (3) effective policy export for sample tenants | Confluence spec; CI test artifacts; internal repo test results | Ethan Park (Control plane) / Jordan Lee (Policy engine) | On release + quarterly spot check | Review precedence rules in spec. Pull 2–3 known policy scenarios and confirm effective output matches the documented rules. Confirm determinism tests exist and are passing in CI for the release tag. |
| Retention enforcement (audit logs) | SOC2 CC7.2, CC7.3; ISO 27001 A.12.4.1, A.12.1.3 | Audit logs are deleted/compacted according to effective retention, with safe, observable jobs and rollback procedures | (1) Enforcement worker runbook; (2) monitoring dashboard screenshot; (3) last-run status (timestamp, deleted rows/partitions); (4) job error budget/alert configuration | Confluence runbook; Observability dashboards; Console enforcement status panel | Kevin Osei (Retention controls) / Sean Gallagher (SRE) | Monthly evidence snapshot + per incident | Confirm enforcement job: runs on schedule, emits metrics (lag, deletes, errors), has rate limiting/safety limits, and supports retries. Validate last successful run within SLA window. Confirm deletion counts are non-zero over time and lag is bounded. |
| Retention enforcement (telemetry/analytics eligible tables) | SOC2 CC7.2; ISO 27001 A.12.1, A.12.4 | Eligible analytics datasets have TTL/partition retention enforced without breaking reporting | (1) Data inventory list of eligible tables; (2) TTL/partition policy config; (3) validation query results for a sample table across a boundary | Data inventory sheet (internal); telemetry pipeline configs; query results attached to evidence pack | Logan Wright (Telemetry) / Mei Lin (Analytics datasets) | Quarterly | Select an eligible dataset. Verify TTL/partition expiry config matches effective policy for the tenant/environment. Run a query showing data older than retention is absent while recent data remains. Validate key dashboards/reports still compute. |
| Audit log coverage: admin + security-relevant actions | SOC2 CC6.2, CC6.6, CC7.2; ISO 27001 A.12.4.1, A.9.4 | Security/admin actions are captured with who/what/when/outcome and are queryable/exportable | (1) Audit event catalog (event types list); (2) sample audit log exports; (3) coverage statement in compliance pack | Confluence audit logging docs; audit-log export service; compliance reporting pack | Marcus Lin (Security Eng) / Hanae Suzuki (Security controls) | Annual + on major feature | Confirm required events exist: retention policy changes, legal hold create/remove, audit export creation, authz/admin changes, key security settings. Validate fields include actor, timestamp, resource, action, result. |
| Audit log export boundaries (retention-aware exports) | SOC2 CC7.2; ISO 27001 A.12.4 | Exports do not promise data beyond retention; exports include metadata/warnings and respect boundaries | (1) Export documentation; (2) example export metadata header; (3) UI text/screenshots indicating retention boundary | Confluence: audit-log retention & exports page; sample export artifacts | Kevin Osei / Markus Klein (Solutions Eng) | Quarterly sample + per customer request | Generate an export for a date range that partially exceeds retention. Confirm export includes only retained data and includes a clear “data may be truncated due to retention” note/metadata. |
| Access control & RBAC for retention/audit functions | SOC2 CC6.1, CC6.2, CC6.6; ISO 27001 A.9.1, A.9.2 | Only authorized roles can change retention, place holds, or export audit logs | (1) RBAC policy doc/role matrix excerpt; (2) API authorization tests excerpt; (3) sample audit events for denied attempts | Confluence RBAC docs; internal authz tests; audit logs | Kaitlyn Nguyen (Authn/Authz) / Jada Williams | Quarterly | Validate role permissions: “Tenant Admin” can set retention within bounds; “Security Admin” can place holds (if enabled); read-only roles cannot change settings; denied attempts are logged. |
| Legal hold process & auditability | SOC2 CC7.2, CC8.1; ISO 27001 A.18.1.3, A.16.1 | Holds can be applied via controlled process; enforcement respects holds; holds are reviewed periodically | (1) Legal holds/exceptions process doc; (2) ticket(s) showing approval workflow; (3) enforcement logs indicating hold prevented deletes; (4) periodic review record | Confluence process page; ticketing system records; enforcement job logs/metrics | Michael Grant (Legal) / Olga Petrov (GRC) | Per hold + semi-annual review | Pick one hold case: verify approvals, scope, and justification. Confirm enforcement job reports “skipped due to hold” for covered datasets. Confirm hold appears in Console as active. Confirm hold is included in periodic review checklist and has an owner. |
| Exception handling for retention deviations | SOC2 CC7.2, CC8.1; ISO 27001 A.16.1 | Retention exceptions are time-bound, approved, documented, and monitored | (1) Exception request template; (2) approved exception ticket; (3) exception expiry review evidence | Confluence process; ticketing system | Olga Petrov / Naomi Feldman | Per exception + quarterly review | Validate exception includes: reason, dataset scope, tenant(s), requested period, compensating controls, approval chain, and expiry. Confirm exception is visible in effective policy view and included in review. |
| Monitoring & alerting for enforcement safety | SOC2 CC7.2, CC7.3; ISO 27001 A.12.1, A.12.4 | Enforcement does not cause customer-impacting instability; monitoring detects lag, errors, and datastore bloat risk | (1) Dashboard links/screenshot; (2) alert definitions (lag, error rate, DB load); (3) incident postmortem linkage if applicable | Observability dashboards; alerting config; incident tracker | Sean Gallagher (SRE) / Allison Grant (Logging standards) | Monthly + post-incident | Confirm alerts exist for: enforcement lag > threshold, deletion errors above threshold, datastore bloat signals, and elevated DB load during deletes. Validate runbook includes mitigation steps and rollback guidance. |
| Change management for retention/audit logging | SOC2 CC8.1; ISO 27001 A.12.1.2 | Significant changes are reviewed, tested, and documented | (1) ADR updates; (2) PR links w/ tests; (3) release notes entry in compliance pack appendix | Confluence ADR; source control PRs; compliance pack | Ethan Park / Connor O’Brien (Release coord) | Per release | Sample a release: verify code reviews, test coverage, and migration notes. Confirm any policy/behavior changes are reflected in documentation and customer-facing statements. |
| Evidence pack generation (repeatability) | SOC2 CC2.1, CC8.1; ISO 27001 A.7.5 (documented information) | Evidence can be generated consistently for audits/customer requests | (1) Compliance reporting pack v1; (2) internal evidence collection runbook; (3) packaged artifacts (zip/pdf) with timestamps | Confluence compliance pack; evidence runbook; secure internal storage location | Daniel Carter (Compliance pack execution) / Olga Petrov | Quarterly + per request | Run the evidence collection procedure for a sample tenant/environment. Confirm outputs are timestamped, access-controlled, and include a manifest listing artifacts and sources. |

---

## Evidence item naming (recommended)
To reduce audit friction, use the following IDs when collecting snapshots:
- **RET-01**: Retention Controls Overview (policy + guardrails)
- **RET-02**: Retention policy schema + precedence spec
- **RET-03**: Effective policy screenshot/export for sample tenant(s)
- **RET-04**: Enforcement last-run evidence (audit logs)
- **RET-05**: Enforcement monitoring dashboard snapshot + alert list
- **AUD-01**: Audit event catalog + coverage statement
- **AUD-02**: Audit log export example + retention boundary metadata
- **HLD-01**: Legal hold case file (approval + verification)
- **EXC-01**: Exception case file (approval + expiry review)

These IDs align with the Compliance Reporting Pack v1 manifest.

---

## How to collect evidence (internal procedure)
1. **Select scope**: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private; region(s); tenant(s) to sample.
2. **Export effective retention policy** from Console (or via admin API) for each sampled tenant.
3. **Capture enforcement status**: last successful run, lag metrics, deletion throughput, and errors.
4. **Generate audit log export samples** (one normal range, one range exceeding retention) and retain export metadata.
5. **Confirm audit coverage**: locate events for retention policy changes and exports; include a sample query or screenshot.
6. **Include exception/hold records** if any exist for the sampled tenants (or include “none in scope” attestation).
7. **Package** artifacts into the Compliance Reporting Pack bundle with a dated manifest.

Access control note: Evidence bundles are **restricted**; share externally only through approved Sales/Solutions process and customer NDA where applicable.

---

## Roles & responsibilities
- **GRC/Compliance (Olga Petrov)**: owns mapping accuracy, evidence procedure, and audit readiness
- **Security Engineering (Marcus Lin / Kevin Osei)**: owns audit log integrity, export behavior, retention enforcement correctness
- **Platform/Control Plane (Ethan Park / Jordan Lee)**: owns policy schema, evaluation correctness, and config persistence
- **Console (Chloe Martin / Jada Williams)**: owns admin UX, APIs, and change auditability
- **SRE (Sean Gallagher / Allison Grant)**: owns monitoring/alerts, operational safety, and incident response linkage
- **Legal (Michael Grant)**: owns legal hold requirements and approvals

---

## Known limitations / customer messaging constraints
- Some infrastructure logs remain governed by standard operational retention and/or vendor limitations; customer-configurable retention may not apply to all streams in v1.
- Retention controls focus on metadata and operational datasets; retention for raw inference payload content is handled separately.
- Private deployments may have deployment-specific storage backends; evidence collection must follow the Private evidence checklist in the reporting pack.

---
